# Kansei ultrasound illustrations

Owner clarification, 29 October 2026: let the tissue painting remain unobstructed
in anatomy mode. Do not cover it with a stack of labels for every tissue layer.
Put supporting anatomical explanations beside or below the image. Use the
independent “Visa fynden” control to reveal the main clinically relevant finding,
with one short label and a restrained pointer placed away from the tissue detail.

Owner clarification, 22 October 2026. The owner selected the near-photographic
biceps tissue preview and requested the same treatment for every published
anatomical layer. The exact approved reference is archived at
`artwork/tissue-realism-20261022/approved-reference.webp`; its original filename
and hash are recorded with each edit. This replaces the earlier saturated
gold/brick-red material palette, while all geometry rules below still apply.

Match lifelike human tissue under soft neutral clinical illumination: pale
cream/straw lobular fat, muted pink/burgundy fine muscle fascicles, delicate
moist translucent ivory/gray fascial laminae, compact pearly tendon collagen,
and pale beige/pink irregular bone trabeculae with a thin ivory cortex and soft
depth fade. Fluid has restrained watery gray depth. Preserve heterogeneous
gray capsular contents as tissue where supplied; do not make them empty fluid.
Keep existing small vessels, tears, calcification and disorganized fibers;
do not add pathology or infer new structures. These remain explanatory
anatomical visualizations, not photographs of a patient or diagnostic images.

Owner clarification, 21 October 2026: fascia is part of the muscle anatomy.
Follow visible intramuscular connective-tissue strands and the larger fascial
planes that separate muscle bellies. Paint them as fine, organically branching
ivory laminae within and between the red fascicles. Preserve the clinician's
boundaries and fiber directions; do not flatten several bellies into one red
slab, replace fascial planes with fat, or turn each white strand into a tendon.

Capsule clarification, 21 October 2026: in a longitudinal joint-recess view,
distinguish the thin capsular boundary from the contents inside it. Do not paint
the entire recess as solid fibrous capsule or a closed collagen cocoon. Preserve
observed gray internal echoes as restrained heterogeneous contents, distinct
from the fibrous wall, without automatically making the recess black fluid.
Do not add a thick second capsule over the cortex or infer active inflammation,
synovial hypertrophy or a particular fluid composition from gray tone alone.

Paint each view continuously. Do not bend material-atlas crops through triangle
meshes, mirror or repeat tiles, or draw ruler-straight fiber bundles. The owner
rejected that method because it introduces rigid corners, seams and unnatural
repetition. Muscle and tendon fibers must curve and vary organically as in the
approved references. Package a whole painting with one global placement only.
Inspect the rendered desktop and mobile images, not just a material swatch.

Cover the complete scan field, including surrounding soft tissue. Do not leave
unpainted grayscale islands around the subscapularis stump or fluid collection.
Use softly fibrous connective tissue where no specific tissue identity has been
established; do not invent extra muscle islands, fat pads, or new lesions. Deep
shadow fades to black, not to uncovered ultrasound pixels.

Keep clinician anatomy contours in the original scan coordinates. A change to
material appearance must not move deltoid boundaries, replace the uneven humeral
cortex with soft tissue, or fill a tendon defect with bone. The subscapularis
example includes a distinct stump and heterogeneous remaining fibers.

Alignment correction, 21 October 2026: do not move a finding marker to compensate
for drift in a painting. Rebuild the painting from the original scan and clinician
contours, then record its single global registration. Check the capsule surface,
cortex and focal notches against the same finding coordinates in original and
anatomy modes, including the enlarged view and both halves of comparison scans.

The painted layer is an explanatory illustration, not a replacement diagnostic
image. Compare each painting against the clinician guide and original before
publication; color samples alone cannot establish anatomical correctness.

Use the shared sequence: original ultrasound, sweeping anatomy, independent
“Visa fynden”, then film when available. Findings use the existing clinic pointer
style and short labels. Do not add a separate multicolor tissue outline system
or color-key legend. Original scan and anatomy must share the same canvas.

Acquisition dates and clock times are hidden across published image views and
thumbnails through an acquisition-header clip, without rescaling or shifting any
clinical pixels. Movies with visible headers use dated-free publication copies,
including fullscreen playback. Original clinical source files are retained.
